summary: The retained endpoint_metrics.json recorded config_split_hash under the older 2-field config-prefix definition and compared it against the training-time 5-field expected constant, producing hash_matches_expected=false. This supplement records both definitions and the independently recomputed digests. The two digests are DIFFERENT; only the dataset bytes are identical between them. The original JSON's comparison was invalid (definition mismatch), not the underlying data.

original_endpoint_json.note: The original file is historical evidence and was NOT modified, regenerated or given any new timestamp. Its false hash_matches_expected flag and measured values stand as recorded.

hash_definitions.shared_computation: h = SHA-256(); h.update(prefix.encode('utf-8')); h.update(train_bytes); h.update(val_bytes); digest = h.hexdigest() (lowercase hex)
hash_definitions.split_bytes: C-contiguous, row-major int64 (8-byte little-endian) raw bytes of train_data.numpy().tobytes() then val_data.numpy().tobytes(); each tensor has shape (4656, 7) so each contributes 260,736 bytes; produced by data.py build_split() (modulus 97, 50% split, vocab 239).

old_two_field.field_order: modulus, train_pct (Python str() of the dict literal, single quotes, insertion order)

training_five_field.field_order: modulus, train_pct, bs, lr, wd (Python str() of the dict literal, single quotes, insertion order; lr serializes as 0.001)
training_five_field.recorded_as: endpoint_metrics.json metadata.split.expected_hash (training-time constant; also carried in every schema-2 full checkpoint as config_split_hash)

hash_definitions.relationship: Both digests hash the SAME generated split bytes with DIFFERENT config prefixes; therefore the two digests are different by construction. An earlier claim that the two hashes were 'identical' was wrong and has been removed from the documentation.

correction.correct_interpretation: The flag compared a 2-field-prefix digest against a 5-field expected constant; the comparison crossed definitions and could never match. The dataset bytes themselves were verified identical by both recomputations.
correction.action: No change to endpoint_metrics.json. Future evaluator outputs record the 5-field definition explicitly (see metadata.split.config_split_hash_definition in new outputs).

measurement_time_note: endpoint_metrics.json carries no explicit measurement timestamp field; its device/library metadata (torch 2.8.0, numpy 2.0.2, python 3.9.6) is unchanged. The creation time above is the time this correction document was written, NOT a measurement time; no measurement timestamp was added to the original JSON.

current_evaluator_source.note: This hash identifies the evaluator source that would generate FUTURE outputs (output_schema_version 2). It is not claimed to be the source that generated the retained endpoint_metrics.json.

verification.method: Independent deterministic recomputation of both digests from data.py build_split() only (dataset construction; no model execution, no inference, no training).
verification.limits: Matching definitions/bytes establishes provenance only: it reconciles the hash-definition mismatch behind the old false flag. It is NOT a new accuracy/loss measurement, NOT an independent replay of training, and NOT a claim that the current evaluator source generated the original JSON. The original measurement values remain exactly as recorded.
